title: Lantern Festival Booth Run-through
description: A six-person team call about a public demo booth, written to sound more like a natural meeting than the harness-oriented Pied Piper fixture. It includes interruptions, corrections, dates, URLs, filenames, issue numbers, and action items. Start times re-flowed against measured Kokoro-82M speech durations so the authored gaps and deliberate overlaps survive real speech.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.text: Morning. Sorry, two goals today: lock the booth run-through for Friday's lantern festival and make sure nobody is still demoing last week's build.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: And please, this time, nobody says beta out loud to the mayor.

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: I fixed the Q R code bug from issue two one four. The iPad was caching the old redirect and making me look cursed.

turns.speaker: ana
turns.text: You did look cursed. Also the sign still says open at five thirty. Doors are at five, soft start at four thirty, right?

turns.speaker: noah
turns.text: Correct. Crew call is four fifteen on Friday, April seventeenth. Public opens at five. Weather says light wind, which is fine unless the paper lantern wall turns into a kite.

turns.speaker: jules
turns.text: I need one clean line for partners. Something shorter than immersive neighborhood story booth with adaptive audio. Nobody can say that while holding noodles.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.text: Use make a tiny night market story, send it to your friends, leave smiling. It is a little corny, but in a good way.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Corny is fine. Corporate is not. We are one folding table away from being a school fundraiser.

turns.speaker: ana
turns.text: Speaking of the table, the final print file is lantern-booth-v7 dot pdf. Please stop opening v5 and asking why the moon mascot looks seasick.

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: Wait, is v7 the one with the bigger Q R code, or the one where the map pin moved?

turns.speaker: ana
turns.text: Bigger Q R code, warmer yellow, less haunted moon.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.text: Good. Ben, walk us through the actual flow as if a stranger walks up with zero context.

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: Okay. They scan the code, land on demo dot lanternlane dot example slash hello, pick three prompts, record a twenty-second story, and get a digital keepsake.

turns.speaker: jules
turns.text: That already sounds better than postcard-style summary. People hear postcard and think printer, and we are absolutely not bringing a printer.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Please God, no printer.

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: Right. After that, the optional text message says your lantern story is ready, not the weird insurance sentence that was stuck in staging.

turns.speaker: noah
turns.text: We still need offline fallback. If the network drops, the staff tablet should open local-demo dot html and save recordings to slash tmp slash lantern slash queue.

turns.speaker: ana
turns.text: Can we not say slash tmp to the public?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Absolutely not. The public gets magic. We get slash tmp.

turns.speaker: jules
turns.text: Also, tiny note, the volunteer script reads like airport safety instructions. Line three says maintain forward queue progress. Nobody talks like that.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.text: Fair. Replace it with if there is a line, invite people to start thinking about their three prompts while they wait.

turns.speaker: noah
turns.text: And add a line about kids. If they are under thirteen, we need the postcard version with no phone number.

turns.speaker: ana
turns.text: I can make that more obvious on screen. Right now the privacy note is technically correct and spiritually invisible.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That is the nicest way anyone has ever called legal text useless.

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: One actual risk. The old audio normalization bug still clips if somebody shouts directly into the iPad. It is way better, not perfect.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.text: How imperfect is not perfect?

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: Festival imperfect, not demo-day imperfect. If someone screams woo into the mic, the waveform gets crunchy for about half a second.

turns.speaker: jules
turns.text: Honestly, that sounds on brand for a lantern festival.

turns.speaker: noah
turns.text: Please write down backup battery counts before we joke ourselves into failure. I have six U S B C packs, two extension reels, and one adapter that everyone will forget.

turns.speaker: ana
turns.text: I am not forgetting the adapter. I am taping it to the table with my name on it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Put my name on it too. Shared custody.

turns.speaker: mira
turns.text: Final checks. Friday, April seventeenth. Crew at four fifteen. Soft start at four thirty. Public at five. Demo U R L demo dot lanternlane dot example slash hello. Print file lantern-booth-v7 dot pdf.

turns.speaker: ben
turns.text: And branch hotfix slash kiosk-offline-two needs review before lunch.

turns.speaker: jules
turns.text: I will rewrite the volunteer sheet in human language and send v3 before eleven.

turns.speaker: noah
turns.text: I will post the load-in checklist in the folder called festival-ops dash final, which means it is definitely not final.

turns.speaker: ana
turns.text: No file named final is ever final.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Great. We are prepared, which is suspicious. End meeting before reality notices.
